WHAT_A1b_CHANGES_AND_WHY_IT_IS_MINE_TO_N.floor_anchored_bars: A1 failed on LEVEL bars that sat ON the hardware read floor. A1b derives them from a co-flown control instead of transcribing them from the ideal — c4230_001 in its seventh costume, applied to bar-setting.
WHAT_A1b_CHANGES_AND_WHY_IT_IS_MINE_TO_N.the_depth_matched_control_is_the_encode_: dropping the two Hs leaves a deterministic codeword whose every pair Lagrange-decodes through the IDENTICAL 9-CX graph and the IDENTICAL frozen decoder, asserted structurally by CX-list equality. The control calibrates the DECODER, like-for-like. That is the matched-conditions rule realised in the cheapest available instrument — no new apparatus.
WHAT_A1b_CHANGES_AND_WHY_IT_IS_MINE_TO_N.MY_OWN_CLAIM_IS_NOW_A_REGISTERED_GATE_TH: Verdict B is the depth-ordering gate: diff = min(floor_s1s2, floor_s1s3) - floor_s2s3, CONFIRMED/REFUTED at ±2se_diff. I read A1's s2s3 as a -2.63σ anomaly, then measured it back to -1.71σ under Whisper's mechanism and stated the one degree of freedom that made my two branches indistinguishable. Registering the ordering BEFORE data is what converts that post-hoc story into something that can be wrong.
WHAT_A1b_CHANGES_AND_WHY_IT_IS_MINE_TO_N.e2e_KA_targets_include_an_UNDERPOWERED_e: ideal counts must grade A=HOLDS and B=UNDERPOWERED — zero depth effect at finite resolution is the noiseless truth. A fence that demanded B=CONFIRMED on ideal data would be demanding an artefact.

what_this_entry_does_NOT_assert: It does NOT assert A1b will pass; the holds can still refuse the flight at submit.

It does NOT assert the depth mechanism is correct — verdict B exists precisely because it is not established.
It does NOT assert my A1 s2s3 reading was right; it was corrected to -1.71σ and is not a finding.
